text:
Hermiston High School students train on reading instruction
Published 9:00 pm Wednesday, October 8, 2025
HERMISTON — Education Pathway students at Hermiston High School recently completed a full-day Enhanced Core Reading Instruction training at the Hermiston School District office.
The reading instruction training is the same as what’s offered to certified educators, according to a press release from the school district. The initiative is a “shining example” of how the district is bringing its “Future Focused” motto to life, the release said. It equipped aspiring teachers with instructional tools and strategies that are typically reserved for experienced professionals.
“Now in its second year, the ECRI training has become a cornerstone of our Education Pathway, giving students the same evidence-based tools and strategies that our teachers use every day,” said Tammy Fisher, family and consumer science teacher at Hermiston High. “This consistency not only prepares students to serve as high-dosage reading tutors, but also ensures they are entering the education profession with a strong foundation in effective literacy instruction.”
Through the training, students were introduced to the Science of Reading framework, building a strong foundation in evidence-based literacy instruction. The framework introduces students to phonics — how letters combine to form different sounds. The training prepared the high schoolers to apply structured, research-driven strategies in their practicum placements and future college coursework, advancing their readiness for careers in teaching.
The hands-on experience is aligned with the district’s Career and Technical Education mission to deliver meaningful, real-world learning. By investing in these future educators, the press release said, Hermiston is helping students take confident steps toward success in the classroom and beyond.
